messages:
mira: Following up on the private/VPC egress tradeoffs: IPv6-only customers + NAT64 semantics are trickier than we modeled. We need a clear stance on guaranteeing source-ip for ACL-driven workloads vs operational cost.

ben: Quick summary: Preserve-src gives good UX for ACLs (no customer changes) but requires either static/reserved egress IPs or an IP mobility layer between cp peering and relay. Both add complexity.

tess: We also saw edge cases where DNS64 causes hostname-level affinity to break when failover changes the source ip (some CDN ACLs rate-limit per-ip).

liam: Practical constraints: relays are autoscaled pools without per-tenant ENIs by default. Adding per-tenant ENIs impacts capacity planning and ENI quota in accounts. ENI attach time can be 15-30s on busy regions.

mira: Options on the table: 
- A: Accept SNAT on failover (simple)
- B: Opt-in reserved IP lease (we provision ephemeral IPs and attach to relay)
- C: IP-mobility proxy that preserves 5-tuple by NAT translation sync between peering and relay

ben: A is easiest and lowest cost. B is middle ground (ops cost + customer opt-in). C is elegant for user transparency but expensive and fragile.

tess: From product: customers fall into two buckets: "ACL-sensitive" and "best-effort". That's a natural opt-in model. We should expose an API flag.

liam: Implementation sketch for B: control-plane issues a lease record: {tenant_id, ip, ttl}. Relay pool watches leases and attachments happen on failover. We'll need to sequence: 1) pre-warm ENI attach 2) BGP/NAT update 3) cut traffic. Pre-warm is painful but possible.

mira: Pre-warm seems necessary to avoid packet loss. But it requires predicting failovers or provisioning on onboarding.

infra-bot: INFO: current relay images support additional ENI mounts; ENI quotas: default 30 per instance-type; attach latency measured at 18s median in us-east-1 yesterday.

ben: On C (ip mobility proxy) we can consider a short-lived L4 proxy that runs at peering and at relay. It keeps session state and rewrites packets so downstream sees same 5-tuple. But we must replicate NAT64 mappings, TTLs, and conntrack semantics. This risks state divergence.

tess: Could we do a hybrid: default A, opt-in B, and an experimental C as an internal feature for top-tier customers?

liam: Agreed. Also need runbooks: if ENI attach fails we must revert to SNAT and alert. That means customers opting into preserve-src must accept occasional failover with SNAT fallback.

mira: Proposed decision: default = SNAT on relay fallback; add API param egress.preserve_src (opt-in) -> provisions ephemeral reserved IPs with SLA caveats; C only for narrow beta.

ben: +1. Please add billing note: reserved IPs billed while lease active and small setup fee.

infra-bot: NOTE: rollout checklist required: quota request templates, automation for pre-warm attach, and monitoring dashboard for attach latency and failure rates.

liam: Action items:
- ben -> draft API schema + pricing blurb
- tess -> product doc for onboarding + test matrix (DNS64, NAT64, long-lived tcp)
- mira -> architecture doc describing lease lifecycle + failover state machine
- infra-bot -> generate ENI quota template and attach metrics collection

mira: Also: include tests for IPv6-only clients with UDP flows (QUIC) since connection migration differs from TCP.

ben: I'll add QUIC scenarios.

liam: If nobody objects I'll mark RFC follow-up decision as: "default SNAT, opt-in preserve-src via reserved IP lease, C=experimental" and file in the architecture tracker by EOD. :thumbsup:

all: no objections.

infra-bot: REMINDER: Any feature that adds ENI churn needs an oncall escalation amendment.
